name: Saint Anthony of Egypt
history: An Egyptian farmer’s son who heard the Gospel read in church, ‘Go, sell what you have and give to the poor’, and did exactly that. He spent the rest of his long life in the desert in prayer and spiritual combat, and so many came to learn from him that he is called the father of monks. Saint Athanasius wrote his life, which helped bring Saint Augustine to conversion.
life: Anthony was about twenty when his parents died, leaving him their land and the care of a younger sister. Moved by the Gospel, he gave away his inheritance, entrusted his sister to a community of consecrated women and began to live as an ascetic near his village. He later shut himself in an old tomb, and then in a ruined fort across the Nile, where for twenty years he struggled in prayer against temptations that Athanasius describes as the attacks of demons. When he came out, people found him calm, healthy and full of kindness. Disciples gathered round him, and the desert, as Athanasius wrote, became a city. In the persecution of 311 he went to Alexandria to encourage the martyrs, and later returned to support Athanasius against the Arians. He spent his last years on a mountain near the Red Sea, where the monastery of Saint Anthony still stands, and died at about a hundred and five.
prayerTo: Saint Anthony, you heard one line of the Gospel and gave your whole life in answer. Pray for me in my temptations, that I may resist them with humility and trust in Christ. Teach me to pray without ceasing, to work with my hands and to find God in silence. Pray for all monks and nuns, and for all who seek Him in the desert of this world. Amen.
penance: Anthony fasted and worked with his hands. Keep a simple meatless day, and do one piece of humble manual work offered as a prayer.
meditation: Anthony saw the snares of the enemy spread over the whole world and asked who could escape them. A voice answered: humility. Where is pride setting a snare for you?
